system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel — Seller Position Review

## Summary verdict: The Seller's draft is the standard commercial position Harbourglass has taken; it departs substantially from Wattlebridge's playbook in nearly every major category. Several positions require explicit pushback before we sign.

---

## Material departures and reasoning

### 1. General warranty cap — Clause 12.1
**Seller: 20% / AUD 4,800,000.**
**Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000 position, with a 20% / AUD 4,800,000 *conditional fallback* requiring prior written authorisation from principal Amelia Frost identifying the specific draft. No such authority exists.

The Seller has simply dropped to its market floor without invoking our fallback gate. That cap binds us *without* Amelia's permission and sits below our strategic baseline. Push back: insist on the 25% / AUD 6M position, or if we later accept 20%, insert the written-authority trigger.

### 2. Thresholds — Clause 12.2
**Seller: de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; seller liable only for excess above basket.**
**Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.

This is the single biggest threshold shift. Two effects: (a) far more claims will clear the de minimis bar, including genuinely small but legally real claims; (b) the basket is dramatically smaller so the cap bites earlier and harder per claim. The Seller's framing ("in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable") is buyer-hostile structurally. Push back: restore both thresholds to the playbook figures; refuse the "excess only" allocation.

### 3. Time limits — Clause 12.3 / 13
**Seller: 18 months general claims, applied to all claims unless expressly stated otherwise.**
**Playbook:** 24 months general; 18-month fallback requires Amelia Frost written approval (none given). Fundamental/title requires six years outside the general bar.

Against our tail, the Seller offers the fallback period *unauthorised*. And extending it to all claims chills fundamental/title claims into the shorter window — exactly what we rejected. Push back: confirm 24 months general and six-year fundamental/title, protect the 18-month fallback as ours.

### 4. Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct
**Seller:** limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance apply to *all* Claims of any nature — no carve-out.
**Playbook:** carve out fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct to the maximum extent enforceable; no one may waive this.

This is a hard legal obligation, not negotiable. There is no carve-out here. Push back: insert the fraud carve-out explicitly and universally, and ensure it cannot be waived or overridden by a qualifier.

### 5. Fundamental / Title regime
**Seller:** capacity and title warranties subject to same caps and time limits as general warranties.
**Playbook:** separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.

Collapsing fundamental/title into the general framework is exactly what we flagged as incompatible with our structural protection. Push back: keep them separate, 100% cap, six-year minimum, free of the thresholds and buyer-knowledge bars.

### 6. Buyer knowledge — Clause 8.3
**Seller:** blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion including any matter discoverable from data room or public records.
**Playbook:** delete entirely; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

Blanket exclusion is the opposite of our position. Push back: delete Clause 8.3 or replace with a narrow, named-persons qualified version. Do not let it absorb fundamental/title or fraud claims.

### 7. Disclosure — Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter
**Seller:** relies on general disclosure of the indexed data room and public registers; nothing admits breach, liability, materiality, loss.
**Playbook:** require *specific fair disclosure*; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure; no admission language.

The Seller is relying on a deemed whole-data-room approach — precisely the sort of disclosure we rejected on DD-006 grounds. Push back: require specific disclosure item by item where relevant; remove the blanket reliance; drop the admission language (or at minimum keep it out of Schedule 7 which defines disclosure scope).

### 8. Bluefen change-control consent — Clause 3 / 6.3
**Seller:** reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of counterparty's written consent.
**Playbook:** effective consent AND evidence conditions are satisfied *before Completion*; reasonable endeavours alone insufficient for a material customer.

A ~AUD 3.6M revenue customer with a formal change-control clause is material. Consent-on-delivery is dangerous because completion can still be blocked. The DD-002 disclosure even concedes no final consent or evidence is included *as at the date of this letter*. Push back: require final written consent executed pre-completion with independent evidence that conditions are satisfied; cap in the SPA; do not accept provisionally.

### 9. Riverlark facility — Clause 2 / 7
**Seller:** release post-Completion from DD-003 (~AUD 3.2M outstanding); discharge of security to follow.
**Playbook:** current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases; a *post*-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

We don't currently know the facility is current, and a post-completion release without our undertaking leaves us exposed if repayment stalls. Push back: confirm facility is fully repaid *before* completion; repayment must come out of Completion funds; a post-completion release requires irrevocable undertaking + Amelia's written approval. Cap Riverlark in the SPA as a condition.

### 10. DD-005 employee bonuses funds-
